standard.title: Improvise, devise and interpret
standard.description: improvise and devise drama, and interpret scripted drama, using elements of drama and conventions to shape and manipulate dramatic action and convey intended ideas, perspectives and/or meaning
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can improvise, devise and interpret scripted drama, manipulating elements and applying conventions relevant to style/form (Y7-8). They can evaluate and refine dramatic work and develop performance skills for specific styles.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students improvise and devise drama, and interpret scripted drama, using elements of drama and conventions to shape and manipulate dramatic action and convey intended ideas, perspectives and/or meaning.

nodes.label: Working within a framework to develop dramatic intention
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use a teacher-provided or self-generated framework to develop a clear dramatic intention — specifying audience, viewpoint, purpose, style and form before devising.
nodes.minimum_width: Student articulates a clear dramatic intention that addresses at least audience, purpose and style/form before beginning devising or interpretation work.
nodes.typical_width: Students use frameworks (stimulus material, imagery, character lists, narrative outlines) to develop drama; they consider contexts such as audiences, viewpoints, intentions, purpose and style/form when planning interpretations; they work collaboratively to devise and develop dramatic action.
wider: Students script scenes initially developed through improvisation, applying play-building techniques to refine them into coherent dramatic work

Students develop devised drama that presents a range of perspectives on an event — using non-linear structures, narrator/chorus conventions, or disruptive characters to challenge 'agreed' understandings
Students devise drama responding to an issue identified from another learning area, building purposeful interdisciplinary dramatic work
nodes.hinge_reason: At Y9-10, devising and interpretation without a clear intentional framework produces technically competent but purposeless work; the aesthetic-choice refinement in the second strand (AC9ADR10C02) depends entirely on having a clear unified intention to refine toward.

response_modes.reason: Require an explicit 'intention statement' before devising work begins — audience, purpose, style, key message. This is not bureaucracy; it is the analytical foundation for all subsequent refining decisions.

success_criteria: Student articulates a dramatic intention addressing audience, purpose and style/form
Student can explain how their devising decisions are driven by that intention

nodes.label: Manipulating elements and conventions to convey meaning
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can select and manipulate elements of drama and conventions to shape dramatic action that conveys intended meaning — including tension, character relationships and symbolic communication.
nodes.minimum_width: Student makes at least three deliberate convention or element manipulation choices that serve their dramatic intention, and can explain each.
nodes.typical_width: Students convey tensions in stories, ideas, characters and relationships through manipulation of language, movement and symbol; they shape dramatic action using props, set items or digital tools; they employ multiple conventions (flashback/flash-forward, chorus, symbol, subtext) to shape meaning and audience experience.
wider: Students explore how non-linear narrative structures — presenting the same story from multiple character perspectives — affect audience experience and meaning
Students use design elements (costume, lighting, set, sound) as integral meaning-making tools, not just support materials
Students investigate conventions from Asian or other cultural dramatic traditions and apply them in their own devising, reflecting on what the conventions carry culturally

response_modes.reason: Students at Y9-10 need a broad repertoire of conventions to draw on; deliberately introduce and practise specific conventions (subtext, beats, chorus, mediatisation) so students can make informed rather than default choices.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of conventions, narrative structures and cultural dramatic traditions available at Y9-10 is very broad; students who build wide convention repertoires can make much more sophisticated and intentional dramatic choices.
success_criteria: Student makes at least three deliberate element or convention choices that serve their dramatic intention
Student can explain what each choice is doing in the drama and how it affects audience experience
Student demonstrates use of at least one convention beyond basic improvisation (e.g. symbol, subtext, non-linear structure, chorus)
